title: The Burning of Briarwell
premise: A village child spends their sister's birthday earning coin for a gift, until bandits put Briarwell to the torch and a stranger from the Heroes' Guild pulls them from the ashes.
description: A short origin story: small kindnesses and small cruelties in a sleepy village, one terrible night, and the road to the Guild. Modeled on the beats of a classic hero-origin opening to validate the authored runtime.
tone: warm pastoral turning to dread; fairy-tale cadence, never grimdark

character_creation.locked_background_prompt: You are a child of about ten growing up in the village of Briarwell, with a gruff, loving father, a patient mother, and a younger sister whose birthday is today.

player_role.name: Child of Briarwell
player_role.premise: You are a village child whose choices today decide what kind of hero you might one day become.
player_role.role_summary: Curious, small, and free to be kind or cruel while the village is still standing.

family_cottage.name: Family Cottage
family_cottage.description: A low thatched cottage that smells of bread and woodsmoke.

village_square.name: Village Square
village_square.description: A well, a notice post, and gossiping neighbours.

market_lane.name: Market Lane
market_lane.description: Old Garrick's stall of sweets, ribbons, and whittled trinkets.

old_mill.name: Old Mill
old_mill.description: The miller's water wheel, and a barn behind it where people meet who should not.

meadow.name: Meadow
meadow.description: Long grass where the village children play, and where Dunstan does his bullying.

woods_edge.name: Woods' Edge
woods_edge.description: A hollow under an old oak at the treeline, a good place to hide.

father.name: Tomas
father.goal: Teach his child that a coin earned honestly is worth more than one taken.

mother.name: Elin
mother.goal: Keep the household warm and the birthday a happy one.

trader.name: Old Garrick
trader.goal: Sell a child something nice for a fair coin.

miller.name: Hob the Miller
miller.goal: Keep his wife from learning about his secret meetings behind the barn.

bandit_leader.name: Red Corwin
bandit_leader.goal: Raid Briarwell and carry off anything, or anyone, worth selling.

guild_master.name: Master Holloway
guild_master.goal: Find a child with the spark of a hero, and get them out alive.

hear_father.title: Listen to Father
hear_father.description: Father has something to ask of you on your sister's birthday.

earn_coins.title: Earn Some Coin
earn_coins.description: Do good turns (or bad ones) around Briarwell to earn coin for Ros's gift. Two will do.

return_doll.title: Bess's Lost Doll
return_doll.description: Little Bess has lost her rag doll somewhere in the village.

miller_secret.title: The Miller's Secret
miller_secret.description: Hob the Miller is up to something behind the barn.

meadow_bully.title: Trouble in the Meadow
meadow_bully.description: Dunstan is picking on the smaller children again.

buy_gift.title: Buy Ros a Gift
buy_gift.description: Spend your coin at Old Garrick's stall.

morning_errand.title: A Birthday Errand
morning_errand.summary: Father asks the child to earn a few coins by honest work and buy Ros a birthday gift.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: a warm family morning, and the birthday errand

village_deeds.title: Good Turns and Bad
village_deeds.summary: The child roams Briarwell. Three villagers need something; each can be helped or exploited for a coin.
village_deeds.objective_text: Earn coin around the village. Help (or don't) Bess, the miller's wife, or the children in the meadow.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: small-village moral choices, each worth a coin
must_mention: the miller sneaking behind the barn
tone_notes: villagers react honestly to kindness and cruelty
a good or bad deed pays the same coin

gift_stall.title: Old Garrick's Stall
gift_stall.summary: The child spends their coin on a birthday gift.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: the market stall and the joy of a first purchase

birthday.title: Ros's Birthday
birthday.summary: Back home at dusk. The child can give Ros the gift, or keep it. As the evening ends, smoke rises from the woods.
birthday.objective_text: Bring the gift home to Ros.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: family warmth at dusk, with the first hint of smoke at the end
tone_notes: let the happy moment land before anything goes wrong

bandit_raid.title: Briarwell Burns
bandit_raid.summary: Night. Red Corwin's bandits torch the village. Father falls defending the door; Mother and Ros vanish in the chaos. The child must decide what to do.
bandit_raid.objective_text: Survive. Hide, fight, or search for your family.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: fire, panic, and a child far too small to stop it
must_mention: Father falling at the cottage door
must_not_reveal: whether Mother and Ros are alive
tone_notes: a child cannot win this fight; fighting ends with the child struck down, not killed

rescue.title: The Stranger in the Ashes
rescue.summary: Master Holloway of the Heroes' Guild finds the child at the woods' edge and offers to take them away.

narrator_contract.scene_focus: grief, smoke, and a hand held out
must_not_reveal: whether Mother and Ros are alive

road_to_guild.title: The Road to the Guild
road_to_guild.summary: Briarwell burns behind them as Master Holloway carries the child toward the Guild. The opening ends here.

intro_sequence.opening_text: Sunlight spills through the cottage shutters in Briarwell. Somewhere in the kitchen your sister Ros is singing, badly, about turning seven.
